a superconducting magnet is safe against burnout if the current in it never exceeds a certain value.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the current density is a more important parameter than the temperature in the determination of the burnout safety condition.
the burnout risk is eliminated if the current is reduced below a certain value before the temperature reaches the critical temperature at some point of the conductor.
the burnout safety condition is not the same as the condition for the absence of a thermal instability in the superconductor.
